_comment: The stamped LINKED tier: how much of the game actually reaches the PC port's
binary. The published LINKED bar counts FUNCTIONS (like MATCHED and CONVERTED),
read from config/port_linked_functions.txt; linkedTus / matchedTus below are the
same build counted in translation units, kept as detail, and are what an older
stamp with no per-function list still reports. This is a STAMP, not a live counter, and it cannot be anything
else from main: port/tools/linkage.py reads build/port/walk_window.map, which only
exists after an MSVC build of the port, and CI on main has no such build.
BEFORE STAMPING, LOOK FOR A BUILD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Every port lane carries its
own build tree, so a current walk_window.map is usually already on disk:
ls -la */build/port/walk_window.map
across the port worktrees, newest first, then run the tool against that root. The
first version of this file was stamped off a five-day-old branch while a map from
the night before sat unread one directory away, and published 26.5% when the real
figure was 34.5%. A stale stamp is still a real measurement, just of the wrong run.
To refresh: `python tools/port_linked_functions.py --root <port tree> --branch <b> --stamp`
rewrites the numbers below AND config/port_linked_functions.txt (the same build, per
function, which tools/chaos_db_ci.py publishes as `linked`) from the tree's own map.
By hand: run `python port/tools/linkage.py [root]` and update the numbers below
together with branch, commit and measuredAt. Never move the count without also
moving the provenance fields - tools/tiers.py drops a stamp missing any of them,
which is the intended behaviour for a number nobody can trace.
basis records what the figure is a measurement OF. The port branches are not merged,
so this is the best single lane rather than a combined total. All seven live lanes,
lk5 3819. Overlapping but not identical seats, so the merged figure is higher and
the published number stays a floor.
LINKED grows when matched TUs become reachable in the port's linked call graph.
Actor methods and free functions both count. Enrollment alone does not increase
the count when the release build still dead-strips the unreachable object.
basis: Integration branch port/h8-int093s at e9e2246f2a6 (the 0.9.3 line), a cold build of walk_window from a clean tree of that commit, measured with port/tools/linkage.py against the map that build wrote (tuatlas1-b1: walk_window linked, 2445 of 2827 exact). The denominator is distinct TU stems in that tree's src/ (2827), not one per function: the port line has folded part of main's one-function files into class TUs, so this figure is NOT comparable with the 2026-09-13 stamp (10595 of 11328, one stem per function) and the percentage fell because the TUs are bigger, not because anything unlinked. It moves again as the port line catches up with main's TU folding (main has 2521 source files, the port line 2827). config/port_linked_functions.txt is the same build seen per function (10957 of the 11389 functions in chaos-db sit in a linked TU), written by tools/port_linked_functions.py. The LINKED bar reads that list: 10957 of 11389 functions (96.2%); linkedTus and matchedTus stay as the unit view of the same build.
